Feign

FAYN -- from Latin fingere ('to shape, form, or fashion falsely'). · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To feign to pretend to have or feel something that one does not actually have or feel.

To avoid an awkward conversation at the reunion, she feigned a phone call and stepped outside.

Worked Example

The poker player feigned disappointment at her cards, sighing dramatically, when in fact she was holding a winning hand.

Notice the SUBJECT here is a person deliberately putting on a false show of emotion -- feign is always about someone's own conscious choice to pretend, unlike Belie, where some detail or fact accidentally gives away the truth.

How Feign Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

simulate

simulate: to imitate or create a false appearance of something

pose

pose: to pretend to be something, or put on a false front, in order to create an effect

Antonyms

reveal

reveal: to make an emotion or fact genuinely known

betray

betray: to unintentionally show a true feeling one meant to hide

How Strong Is It? — pose → simulate → feign

pose vs. feign

pose vs. feign: He posed as a wealthy investor to gain access to the private auction, using an expensive suit and a fake business card.

simulate vs. feign

simulate vs. feign: The training program used a flight simulator to simulate a full engine failure at takeoff.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — fei-/fic-

root — fei-/fic-: to shape, form, or fashion (often falsely) (Latin (fingere))

Put it together

Put it together: Feign traces back to the Latin verb fingere, 'to shape or fashion' -- often in the sense of shaping a false impression. To feign something is to 'fashion' a fake version of an emotion or condition.

Use the root in a new word: feint

Use the root in a new word: feint: The boxer threw a feint with his left hand to distract his opponent before landing a real punch with his right.

Root Check

Word Choice

Feign is always about a person's own deliberate act of pretending. Compare Belie, where some involuntary detail -- a tone, an expression -- contradicts the truth without anyone consciously acting. 'She feigned surprise' is a choice; 'her face belied her surprise' is an involuntary giveaway.
